prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1199; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officer narrative: Pearland, Texas. Responding to a report of a low-speed head-on collision between two passenger vehicles on a two-lane roadway. Driver 1 was operating the vehicle that sustained the most visible front-end damage and reported neck pain consistent with whiplash. Driver 2 stated the vehicles made contact after a brief loss of lane control by the other driver. A Passenger was seated in Driver 1's vehicle and was present during the collision. Officers observed that the damage pattern is largely consistent with the reported impact. Scene photographs confirm the positions of both vehicles and the areas of contact. No independent witnesses were located at the scene. Driver 1 identified the owner of the vehicle as the policyholder, and Driver 1 reported living in the same household. No prior damage to either vehicle was observed or reported. The injury Driver 1 described is consistent with the type and force of this collision. This report is submitted for review.
